expectations.name: 01-record-written
expectations.text: A decision record is written under docs/adrs/.

expectations.name: 02-structure
expectations.text:
Each page the agent wrote or changed meets the map's structural rules: a declared kind, listed in its guide, links
and anchors that resolve, the kind's sections in order, a record named NNNN-<slug>.md, no rejected synonym.

expectations.name: 03-lead
expectations.text: The record opens with a lead under its title, not a restatement of the title.

expectations.name: 04-context-tells-what-happened
expectations.text:
The record's Context tells what happened, the incident with Redis evicting queued jobs and what it cost, before it
states a conclusion such as "we need a durable queue".
expectations.evidence: Context opens with the incident before any conclusion: "Nadia reported on March 4 that 300 members had paid but received no receipt since Saturday. The Redis server had run out of memory and evicted keys, including Celery's queued receipt jobs, without logging an error. Nadia resent the receipts by hand from the orders table." It then states "Redis served only the job queue, and Tom was the only volunteer who knew how to restore it" and names the forces: "protect queued jobs from the loss seen in this incident, allow a pantry order and its job to commit together, and reduce the services volunteers maintain." No conclusion like 'we need a durable queue' appears in Context.

expectations.name: 05-decision-names-the-product
expectations.text: The record's Decision names procrastinate, the product chosen.
expectations.evidence: match /## Decision\s.*procrastinate/ in ['docs/adrs/0002-keep-background-jobs-in-postgres.md']: {'docs/adrs/0002-keep-background-jobs-in-postgres.md': '## Decision\n\nKeep background jobs in Postgres, using procrastinate'}
